sections.html:
Autauga County names Prattville as its seat, yet the city spills over into Elmore County as well. Montgomery lies southeast of it, and the city is counted in that metro area. Roughly 36 square miles make up the city, at an elevation near 276 feet. Interstate 65 passes east of downtown with exits 179 and 181 inside the Elmore County portion. Downtown Montgomery is 14 miles southeast along that highway, and Birmingham is 82 miles north.

For a seller the county line is practical. Your parcel's county can decide the school system for the address and the office that holds your records, so find out before the house goes on the market.

Prattville had 37,781 residents in 2020 and an estimate of 40,582 for 2025, a rise of 7.4 percent.

In 2020 the census found 14,624 households in 15,537 housing units, with 5.9 percent of the units vacant. Vacancy among owner homes was 1.3 percent and among rentals 5.9 percent. Steady growth means new subdivisions sit alongside very old streets by the former mill district, where a house can be a hundred years old or more.

sections.h2: Older homes near the mill district
sections.html: The city grew around cotton mills powered by Autauga Creek, and the Daniel Pratt Historic District, Bell House and Buena Vista are on the National Register of Historic Places. A house near downtown may carry decades of postponed work, and buyers who need a loan often insist it be repaired first. Inspectors on older homes pay particular attention to wiring, plumbing and roofs.

The Autauga County part of Prattville belongs to the Autauga County School System, which has eight schools in the city, including Prattville High School and the Autauga County Technology Center. The Elmore County part is in the Elmore County Public School System. Prattville Christian Academy and Autauga Academy are private schools in the city.

One city, two districts: the county line decides. Phone the district office to verify an address before telling a buyer where a child would attend.

Interstate 65, U.S. 31, U.S. 82 and State Route 14 all pass through the city. U.S. 82 runs south with I-65 toward Montgomery and leads northwest 89 miles to Tuscaloosa. A small airport lies about 3.5 miles from downtown, and Autauga County Rural Transportation runs dial-a-ride service.

High Point Town Center, a large shopping center built in 2007 and 2008, and the Capitol Hill golf courses on the Robert Trent Jones Golf Trail are common selling points for houses nearby.

An EF3 tornado hit Prattville on February 17, 2008. It destroyed more than 45 homes and businesses and damaged over 700 others. Twenty-nine people were hurt and none died.

If your house was repaired after that storm, hold on to the permits, contractor invoices and insurance records, since a buyer or inspector could request them. Any storm damage you never fixed, a roof or a wall for example, should be disclosed up front, because inspections tend to find it.

The annual tax bill is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. Closing in the fall or winter means the contract should say who settles the balance.

Alabama Code section 40-22-1 bars recording a deed until its recordation tax is paid. The tax is 50 cents on each $500 of value, or part of $500. The state keeps two thirds, the county gets one third, and the recording fee is charged separately.

The law also calls for proof of the real sale price, on a Department of Revenue form. A person who knowingly refuses that proof when asked, or supplies a false one, owes the greater of $100 or 25 percent of the tax. Hand the closing agent an accurate contract and the issue never comes up.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes or a loan owed
sections.html:
Money owed does not stop a closing. Your lender writes a payoff letter, the county reports the tax balance, and the closing agent settles both from the sale price. Send the tax request to the Elmore County office when the house sits in that part of the city, and to Autauga County otherwise.

The title report may also list liens, utility arrears and code fines, which are paid off at the table. Ask to see the report early. Then your net proceeds are no surprise when the date is set.

Cash appeals to owners who need a closing date they can count on, or who cannot face weeks of showings. These are the usual situations here:

  • An aging house by the historic district with roofing, wiring or plumbing needs.
  • A rental whose last tenant left damage to fix.
  • An inherited house in either Autauga or Elmore County.
  • A family relocating for work toward Montgomery or Birmingham on a short timetable.

Here is how it goes. You describe the property and we respond with a number. Say yes, and a title company or attorney verifies who owns it, arranges payoffs and agrees a closing day with you. At closing, bring photo identification, the deed or estate papers and any lease. We buy Prattville houses as they are, and you may weigh our offer against a listing plan before deciding.

On the closing date you meet the closer, in person or by mail with a notary, and sign the deed and the settlement statement. The closer records the deed with the probate office, pays the recordation tax and fee, clears any mortgage and tax balance, and sends you the remainder. Read the settlement statement line by line before signing, and ask about any charge that you do not recognize.

If someone lives in the house, agree on a move-out date in writing. Keys and garage openers change hands at closing. Before you leave, cancel or transfer utilities, forward your mail and photograph the empty rooms.

If you inherited the house, begin by confirming who has legal authority to sign, because no closing can happen until that is clear. The probate office or an attorney can tell you what paperwork is needed, and it is better to learn this before you ask for offers, since missing paperwork can hold up an inherited sale for weeks.

If tenants live there, hand over the lease and the rent record. Some buyers will close with the tenant in place, and others want the house empty. Choose the timing that fits your situation and say so in the first conversation.

Some steps pay off on either route. Collect the deed, this year's tax bill and any storm or repair records. Remove trash, keep utilities on so systems can be tested, and write down which fixtures and appliances stay.

Be upfront about problems. A buyer who finds a leak or a cracked slab after promising a price may walk away or ask for a lower one, and surprises waste everyone's time.

faqs.a: Autauga County, where Prattville is the seat. A section of the city is in Elmore County.
Industrialist Daniel Pratt founded the town in 1839 along Autauga Creek.

faqs.q: How far is Prattville from Montgomery?
faqs.a: Interstate 65 leads about 14 miles southeast from the city to downtown Montgomery.

faqs.q: When are Prattville property taxes due?
Can I sell a Prattville house with storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Roof and storm damage do not stop a sale, since we buy as is.
